cards.front: When do you use the preterite in a sports context?
cards.back:
Use the preterite (pretérito indefinido) for:

- Completed, one-time events: Ganamos el partido.
- Actions with a clear start/end: Jugué dos horas.
- Sequences of events: Llegué, calenté y jugué.
- Scores and results of finished games: Perdimos 11-9.
cards.grammarNote: The preterite is the 'narrative' past tense — perfect for recounting a game that is over and done.

cards.front:
Preterite endings — regular -AR verbs
(e.g., jugar, ganar, marcar)
cards.back:
yo         -é         jugué
tú         -aste      jugaste
él/ella    -ó         jugó
nosotros   -amos      jugamos
vosotros   -asteis    jugasteis
ellos      -aron      jugaron
cards.grammarNote: NOTE: The nosotros preterite (-amos) looks identical to the present. Context (like ayer) clarifies which tense is meant.

cards.front:
Preterite endings — regular -ER / -IR verbs
(e.g., perder, correr, salir)
cards.back:
yo         -í         perdí
tú         -iste      perdiste
él/ella    -ió        perdió
nosotros   -imos      perdimos
vosotros   -isteis    perdisteis
ellos      -ieron     perdieron
cards.grammarNote: -ER and -IR verbs share the same preterite endings. Note the accent marks on yo and él/ella forms.

cards.back:
yo gané
tú ganaste
él/ella ganó
nosotros ganamos
vosotros ganasteis
ellos/ustedes ganaron
cards.grammarNote: ganar is regular in the preterite. 'Ganamos el torneo' (We won the tournament) uses the nosotros form.

cards.back:
yo perdí
tú perdiste
él/ella perdió
nosotros perdimos
vosotros perdisteis
ellos/ustedes perdieron
cards.grammarNote: perder is regular in the preterite despite being stem-changing in the present. Stem changes do NOT apply in the preterite for -ER verbs.

cards.front: jugar — preterite spelling change in yo form
cards.back:
yo jugué  (NOT jugé)

All other forms are regular:
tú jugaste, él jugó, nosotros jugamos…
cards.grammarNote: Verbs ending in -gar change g→gu in the yo preterite to preserve the hard /g/ sound before -é.

cards.front: practicar — preterite spelling change in yo form
cards.back:
yo practiqué  (NOT practiqué with a hard c)

All other forms are regular:
tú practicaste, él practicó, nosotros practicamos…
cards.grammarNote: Verbs ending in -car change c→qu in the yo preterite to preserve the hard /k/ sound before -é.

cards.front: ser / ir — irregular preterite (both are identical!)
cards.back:
yo fui
tú fuiste
él/ella fue
nosotros fuimos
vosotros fuisteis
ellos/ustedes fueron
cards.grammarNote: ser and ir have the same preterite forms — context tells them apart. 'Fue un partido increíble' (It was an incredible match) uses ser.
ganamos is the nosotros preterite of ganar. 'Ayer' confirms this is past, not present.

cards.front: Jeffrey lost the first game but won the second.
cards.back: Jeffrey perdió el primer juego, pero ganó el segundo.
cards.grammarNote: Both verbs are in the él preterite. This sentence narrates a sequence of results in a completed match.

cards.front: I played pickleball for two hours.
cards.back: Jugué al píckleball durante dos horas.
cards.grammarNote: jugué (yo preterite) + durante + time span describes a completed activity with a defined duration.

cards.front: My brother scored the last point.
cards.back: Mi hermano anotó el último punto.
cards.grammarNote: anotó is the él preterite of anotar (regular -ar). 'Último' means 'last'; it follows the noun here for emphasis.

cards.front: Common time markers that signal the preterite
cards.back:
ayer — yesterday
anteayer — the day before yesterday
el lunes pasado — last Monday
la semana pasada — last week
el año pasado — last year
una vez — once
en 2023 — in 2023
de repente — suddenly
cards.grammarNote: These words point to a completed, bounded event in the past — a strong signal to use the preterite.

cards.front:
Put this sports recap into the preterite:
'We arrive, we warm up, we play, and we win.'
cards.grammarNote: All four verbs in the nosotros preterite. For -ar verbs, nosotros preterite = nosotros present, so the sentence reads naturally.

cards.front: correr (to run / to race) — full preterite
cards.back:
yo corrí
tú corriste
él/ella corrió
nosotros corrimos
vosotros corristeis
ellos/ustedes corrieron
cards.grammarNote: correr is a regular -er verb in the preterite. 'Corrí diez kilómetros ayer' = I ran ten kilometers yesterday.
